clue.text: Tintin's dance?

parts.note: read Tintin as tin plus tin, and tin is another word for a can, so a doubled can names the high-kicking dance

explanation.surface: A question about what dance the boy reporter of the comic books might do.
explanation.walkthrough: The cartoon reporter is a red herring: split his name into TIN TIN, swap each tin for its synonym CAN, and you get the Parisian dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a lively high-kicking French music-hall routine, so it is a dance.

clue.text: Emerged from a flower

parts.note: a rose is a familiar garden flower

explanation.surface: Something came out of a bloom, like an insect crawling from petals.
explanation.definitionFit: To have come up or appeared is the past tense of arise, matching emerged.

clue.text: Get 50% off wrapping material that comes with strings attached

indicators.note: taking half away leaves only the first five of the ten letters of the wrapping word

parts.note: cellophane is a clear film used for wrapping

explanation.surface: A shopper is offered half price on packaging, with a catch attached to the deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with strings attached' looks like the idiom for a catch in a deal; here it is literal, an instrument fitted with strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a bowed instrument fitted with four strings, so it literally comes with strings.

clue.text: Scrooge endlessly drawing back

indicators.note: back says the shortened word is read in reverse order
without its end, the last letter of the word for drawing is lost

parts.note: dragging is drawing along, as in pulling a load

explanation.surface: A miser keeps drawing back from paying, as Scrooge would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims DRAGGING to DRAGGIN, which 'back' then turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrooge is a mean, tight-fisted person, as is a miser or skinflint.

clue.text: I'm sorry name-drop is inappropriate

indicators.note: inappropriate suggests the letters of the fodder are out of their proper places and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone apologises after dropping a famous name at the wrong moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inappropriate' rearranges the letters of NAME-DROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite apology or request to repeat, expressing regret just like a mumbled apology does.

clue.text: Writer one charged to invest bit of spare cash for retirement

indicators.note: to invest here means to put something inside, so one letter goes into the middle

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

indicators.note: a bit of the word spare is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A writer is told to put a little spare money aside for old age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged' tempts you towards money or accusation; it is the physics sense, an atom with an electric charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension is a regular income paid to someone who has stopped working.

clue.text: Sends back chap entering Red Square

indicators.note: entering means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: taken as the colour word as written
a chap is a man
S is an abbreviation for square, as in street names

explanation.surface: A man walks into the famous square in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Square, the Moscow landmark, is split into two separate pieces; the chap enters only the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A court remands an accused person, returning them to custody until a later hearing.

clue.text: Living dangerously, I hint about bungs in the past

indicators.note: to bung is to shove or toss, so the rearranged letters are tossed into the middle of another word

parts.note: once means at some earlier time

indicators.note: about signals the letters of the two words are turned around and mixed

explanation.surface: Someone hints at having taken bribes long ago, which is risky to admit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungs' looks like bribes, a sly misdirection; here it means shoves in. 'about' mixes the letters of hint into THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on thin ice is an idiom for being in a risky or precarious position.

clue.text: Second cure-all made up of groups of atoms

parts.note: a mo is a brief moment, a second

indicators.note: made up suggests the letters are invented or put together anew, an anagram

explanation.surface: A miracle remedy is concocted in a moment, like a chemist's instant fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges CURE-ALL to give LECULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecules are bonded groups of atoms, so the adjective describes things relating to them.

clue.text: Tough Dundee player downs cooking oil

indicators.note: to down is to swallow, so one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: Paul Hogan played the lead role in the film Crocodile Dundee

indicators.note: cooking implies the letters are being worked on and changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A Scottish footballer from Dundee gulps down cooking oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dundee player' suggests the Scottish football club; it is the actor who played Crocodile Dundee. 'cooking' turns OIL into OLI, which HOGAN downs.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough is a rough, violent young man, the same as a thug or lout.

clue.text: Some elements of roofing material put back after vandalism — at last

indicators.note: after says the reversed piece comes behind the other in the answer
at last picks only the final letter of vandalism
put back says the word for roofing material is read in reverse

parts.note: slate is a stone split into tiles for roofs

explanation.surface: Roofing parts are replaced after vandals have struck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' sounds like repairing a roof after vandals; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, copper and gold are metals, which form a large class of chemical elements.

clue.text: Embellishment of Christmas speech?

parts.note: Christmas falls in December, abbreviated Dec
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A seasonal address, perhaps the monarch's Christmas broadcast, is dressed up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament or adornment added to make something more attractive is an embellishment.

clue.text: It's very easy to scratch head and part of foot

indicators.note: to scratch the head is to remove the first letter of the word

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy

explanation.surface: Scratching your head and then your foot is simple enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of foot' is a unit of length, not anatomy: a twelfth of a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: There are twelve of these units in an imperial foot of length.

clue.text: Some fishermen had enough fish

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The anglers have caught their fill for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes the letters hidden in fisherMEN HAD ENough.
explanation.definitionFit: The menhaden is an oily North American sea fish of the herring family.

clue.text: Internal parts of radio spilled over surface

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the hidden run is read upwards, backwards
the inner letters of the phrase supply a hidden run, skipping its ends

explanation.surface: Something spills out of a radio's innards onto a table top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Internal parts of' hides DIOSPILLE inside raDIO SPILLEd and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry this is a closed curved surface every plane section of which is an ellipse.

clue.text: The distraught nurses battle over revelatory announcement

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece holds another inside it
distraught means upset, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several First World War battles
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Upset nurses fight on before something is finally revealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges the three letters into HET. 'nurses' looks like the hospital staff but means holds. Ypres is a Belgian town fought over in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's exclamation when a trick is revealed, announcing the surprise.

clue.text: Started to carry large screen

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: shied means started or jumped back in fright, as a horse does
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone began lugging a big screen around.
explanation.definitionFit: A shield is something that protects or hides, as a screen does.

clue.text: Misbehave in performance, getting excited

parts.note: a play is a stage performance
up can mean excited, as in being keyed up

explanation.surface: An actor behaves badly on stage, getting carried away.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up or be naughty is to misbehave, as children or machines do.

clue.text: Caustic Tim Vine?

definitions.meaning: biting or sharp, as a remark or smell can be
Tim Vine is a British comedian famed for rapid one-liner puns

explanation.surface: Is the comedian Tim Vine a cutting wit?
explanation.walkthrough: Tim Vine, a British stand-up famous for punning one-liners, is split as PUN GENT, a man of puns; the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent remark is sharply biting and critical, just like a caustic one.

clue.text: Develops supporting structures to protect one

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: piers are pillars or supports, as under a bridge

explanation.surface: Builders develop supports to shield a single item.
explanation.definitionFit: To be first to develop or introduce something new is to pioneer it.

clue.text: Allow to stay with no backing, being exploited

parts.note: to put someone up is to give them a bed for the night

indicators.note: backing says the word no is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A guest is allowed to stay without support and so is taken advantage of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no backing' reads like lacking support; 'backing' is the reversal signal on no.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put-upon is taken advantage of or imposed on by others.

clue.text: Difficult individual runs America, grasping nothing

indicators.note: grasping means holding, so the letters close round another piece

parts.note: one means a single individual
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
US stands for United States, America
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A tricky person runs the United States while holding nothing in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and hard to carry out.

clue.text: Strikes back in skirmish

indicators.note: back says the word for strikes is read in reverse

parts.note: raps are sharp blows or knocks

explanation.surface: A fighter hits back during a small fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or argue in a minor way, as a skirmish is a minor clash.

clue.text: Extremely low number returned drinking flask

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the reversed piece holds another inside
returned says the number word is read backwards

parts.note: ten is a number
a Thermos is a vacuum flask, from the brand name

explanation.surface: A very low figure returns, swigging from a flask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives NET; Thermos is a brand name that became the everyday word for a vacuum flask.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest of all, the furthest down, so it is extremely low.

clue.text: Earth is boring planet for adult females

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Mars is the fourth planet

explanation.surface: Our planet finds the red planet dull, for female reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Mares are grown-up female horses, so they are adult females of that animal.

clue.text: Team will reportedly move furtively

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are to be heard as spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a side is a team, and will contracts to 'll, giving side'll

explanation.surface: A team will creep around on the pitch, says the report.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along sideways, stealthily or nervously.

clue.text: Occasionally throw out usable beds in a dishevelled state

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every third letter of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Someone throws out beds that could still be used, leaving the place a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Occasionally' takes every third letter, starting from the first: Throw Out Usable beds gives T, O, U, S, L, E.
explanation.definitionFit: A tousle is a rumpled, untidy mass, as of hair, so it is a messy condition.

clue.text: Turkey welcomed into swelling European project

indicators.note: welcomed into means one piece is let in inside the other

parts.note: proud can mean swelling above a surface, as in proud flesh
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: Turkey is admitted to an expanding scheme for the European bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun (a scheme); it is the verb, to stick out.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to stick out or jut, which is one sense of project as a verb.

clue.text: Education unfortunately not working, hampering millions in city

indicators.note: hampering means hemming in, so the letters close around one more
unfortunately suggests the word is mangled into a new order

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Failing schools are holding back a city's millions in funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the three letters of not; 'hampering' sets M inside the chain, straight after the abbreviation for education.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital of the Canadian province of Alberta, and a London district.

clue.text: Nurse about to abandon opposing figure

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so a piece is taken out of the word

parts.note: a resister is someone who opposes
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A nurse is about to walk away from a figure who opposes her.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior nurse in a British hospital ward is traditionally called a sister.
